plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A hybrid flowering cherry tree that produces dense clusters of delicate, slightly fragrant five-petaled blossoms before the leaves emerge. It is the iconic tree of hanami celebrations and is widely planted in parks and along waterways.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate regions worldwide; in northern Japan and higher elevations it peaks in April
plants.funFact: The original Yoshino cherry trees in Washington D.C. were a gift from Tokyo in 1912, and all Yoshino cherries are thought to descend from a single original tree propagated by grafting.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A native European perennial bulb with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers and gray-green strap-like leaves. It grows in woodlands, meadows, and grassy banks, and its many cultivars are staples of spring gardens.
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the UK, France, and Belgium; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodil bulbs contain lycorine and galantamine; galantamine is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose clusters of pea-like magenta-pink flowers burst directly from branches and trunk before heart-shaped leaves appear. It thrives in woodland edges and is a favorite native ornamental that supports early pollinators.
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, northern Mexico
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a tangy flavor, and the trees show cauliflory, meaning flowers grow straight from woody trunks and older branches.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Not a spring bloomer in the north, this tree is in its late-blooming tail in parts of the Southern Hemisphere and in tropical highlands, but its relative spring display in lower-latitude regions makes it a notable April bloomer in places like Kenya, northern India, and parts of Florida and the Caribbean.
plants.bloomingSeason: Variable: October to December in the Southern Hemisphere; April to June in the northern subtropics
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Kenya, India, Florida, and Mediterranean-type climates
plants.funFact: A carpet of fallen jacaranda blossoms is considered a spectacle in cities such as Pretoria, which is nicknamed the Jacaranda City.
